title: Oxford University Research Officer Job 2026: Fully Funded International Development Career Opportunity at OPHI (Apply by 14 August 2026)
summary: The University of Oxford has opened applications for an exciting Research Officer position within the Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) . This prestigious opportunity offers experienced researchers the chance to contribute to global poverty reduction by working with the internationally recognized Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) . The successful candidate will work alongside renowned poverty researcher Dr. Sabina Alkire , Director of OPHI, supporting governments, international organizations, and policy institutions in implementing multidimensional poverty measurement systems that influence development policy across the world. This role is ideal for candidates with strong quantitative research expertise, experience in economics or social policy, and a passion for using evidence-based research to improve the lives of people globally. Application Deadline: 12:00 Midday (UK Time), Friday, 14 August 2026 About the University of Oxford The University of Oxford is one of the world s oldest and most respected universities, consistently ranked among the top higher education institutions globally. Its research influences policy, innovation, and academic advancement across numerous disciplines. Within Oxford, the Department of International Development (ODID) is internationally recognized for producing world-class research that addresses poverty, inequality, humanitarian crises, governance, migration, education, health, and sustainable development. One of ODID s flagship research initiatives is the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) , whose work has transformed how governments measure and understand poverty worldwide. About the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) The Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) is a globally respected research center dedicated to improving the measurement of poverty beyond income alone. Rather than focusing only on financial resources, OPHI develops Multidimensional Poverty Indices (MPI) that evaluate deprivation across several aspects of life, including: Education Health Housing Living standards Nutrition Employment Access to essential services Governments, UN agencies, development banks, and policy organizations rely on OPHI s methodologies to design more effective poverty reduction strategies. As a Research Officer, you will directly contribute to these globally influential initiatives. About the Research Officer Position The Research Officer will become an important member of OPHI s multidisciplinary research team. Reporting directly to Dr. Sabina Alkire , the successful candidate will help governments and international institutions implement multidimensional poverty measures and use them to guide evidence-based policymaking. The position combines: Academic research International collaboration Government advisory work Statistical analysis Capacity building Policy implementation International travel It offers a rare opportunity to bridge academic excellence with practical development impact. Key Responsibilities Successful applicants will undertake a wide range of technical and research responsibilities. 1. Support Governments and Institutions The Research Officer will assist governments and partner organizations in implementing multidimensional poverty measurement systems. Responsibilities include: Designing national multidimensional poverty measures Updating existing multidimensional poverty indices Validating national poverty methodologies Advising policymakers Supporting implementation strategies 2. Deliver Technical Assistance The successful candidate will provide expert technical support to governments, think tanks, and international organizations by: Conducting online training sessions Organizing in-person workshops Delivering technical presentations Guiding institutional partners throughout implementation processes 3. Conduct High-Level Research The Research Officer will actively contribute to OPHI s academic research by: Writing publishable academic papers Conducting quantitative analysis Developing new methodologies Investigating multidimensional poverty trends Producing research outputs for international audiences 4. Calculate and Analyze Poverty Indices The role includes extensive statistical analysis using multidimensional poverty data. The successful candidate will: Estimate multidimensional poverty indices Analyze large datasets Interpret research findings Produce policy-relevant evidence 5. Participate in Academic Activities Research Officers will become active participants in OPHI s academic community through: Research workshops Academic seminars Conferences Collaborative research projects Professional presentations Contract Duration The appointment is initially offered for: One-year contract The role is expected to begin: As soon as possible International Travel This position includes significant international engagement. Successful applicants should be prepared to travel overseas for up to: 90 days per year Travel will support: Government partnerships Capacity-building workshops International collaborations Technical assistance missions Travel remains subject to any applicable travel restrictions. Required Qualifications Applicants should possess one of the following: PhD/DPhil in Economics PhD/DPhil in Social Policy PhD/DPhil in another quantitative social science Equivalent professional experience in a related field Candidates should also demonstrate a strong quantitative background. Essential Technical Skills Applicants must possess excellent technical competencies, including: Statistical Programming Excellent knowledge of: STATA (essential) Computer Skills Strong proficiency in: Microsoft Office Data analysis Statistical computing Research Skills Candidates should have experience with: Quantitative research Policy analysis Statistical modelling Data interpretation Academic writing Essential Personal Skills The University of Oxford is seeking candidates who demonstrate: Excellent interpersonal skills Cross-cultural communication abilities Strategic policy engagement Professional discretion Ability to collaborate across disciplines Ability to work across different time zones Strong organizational skills Professional communication Working Environment at ODID The Oxford Department of International Development places significant emphasis on creating an inclusive and supportive workplace. ODID welcomes applicants from all backgrounds and actively promotes: Equality Diversity Inclusion Respect Cultural understanding The department recognizes the impact of social inequalities and continues to implement organizational improvements that foster fairness and equal opportunity. Equality and Diversity Commitment Oxford University emphasizes that all eligible candidates are encouraged to apply. The department: Holds an Athena Swan Bronze Award Promotes organizational equality Encourages diversity Works to reduce bias and discrimination Supports inclusive research and teaching environments This commitment reflects Oxford s broader mission of strengthening global development research through diverse perspectives. Application Process Applications must be submitted online. Applicants will need to upload: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Supporting Statement Only these two documents will be considered during the shortlisting process. Any additional uploaded documents will not be reviewed. APPLY HERE Tips for Preparing a Strong Application To maximize your chances of success: Highlight your quantitative research experience. Demonstrate expertise in STATA programming. Showcase experience working with governments, international organizations, or policy institutions where applicable. Include publications, research projects, and statistical analysis experience. Emphasize cross-cultural collaboration and international engagement. Tailor your supporting statement to explain how your experience aligns with OPHI s mission of multidimensional poverty measurement. Why This Opportunity Is Exceptional Working with OPHI provides researchers with the opportunity to influence global development policy at the highest level. Benefits include: Working at the University of Oxford Collaborating with internationally recognized researchers Contributing to globally influential poverty measurement methodologies Publishing high-impact academic research Supporting governments around the world Participating in international workshops and collaborations Building a strong international research network For professionals interested in development economics, poverty research, public policy, and quantitative social science, this role represents an outstanding career opportunity. Visit HERE to learn more about the Oxford University Research Officer Job 2026. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted before 12:00 Midday (UK Time) on Friday, 14 August 2026 . Late applications will not be considered. Interested applicants should prepare their CV and supporting statement well before the closing date to avoid last-minute technical issues. Conclusion The University of Oxford s Research Officer position within the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced quantitative researchers to contribute directly to international development policy and poverty reduction efforts worldwide. By combining rigorous academic research with real-world policy implementation, the successful candidate will help governments and institutions develop multidimensional poverty measures that improve decision-making and enhance people s lives. With opportunities for international collaboration, research publication, technical training, and policy engagement, this role is an ideal next step for researchers seeking to make a meaningful global impact. Applicants who meet the qualifications are encouraged to submit their applications before the 14 August 2026 deadline. title: EU Environment Academy 2026 in Ukraine: Fully Funded Training on EU Environmental Law and Accession
summary: Applications are now open for the EU Environment Academy 2026–2027, an intensive professional training programme supporting environmental governance and Ukraine’s integration of European Union environmental legislation. Ukraine will host the 2026 edition of the Academy, which is organised and fully funded by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency. The programme will help environmental professionals, government officials, civil-society representatives and selected advanced university students strengthen their understanding of EU accession, environmental law and the requirements contained in Chapter 27 of the EU acquis. The Academy will run approximately from late September 2026 until March 2027, including a winter break. Most activities will be delivered online, with the possibility of one or two in-person study visits or workshops in relevant European Union Member States. Applications must be submitted by 20 August 2026, according to the official EU Environment Academy 2026 announcement . About the EU Environment Academy 2026 The EU Environment Academy provides advanced knowledge of European Union institutions, legislation, policymaking, enlargement and accession. The 2026–2027 programme has been developed specifically in the context of Ukraine’s European integration process. One of the central areas of study will be Chapter 27 of the EU acquis, which covers environmental protection and related legislation that countries seeking EU membership must incorporate into their national legal and administrative systems. The programme will examine: The institutions, bodies and agencies of the European Union; The relationship between EU institutions and national authorities; EU treaties, directives, regulations and other legal instruments; The EU policymaking and lawmaking process; The EU enlargement and accession process; Legal approximation and legislative alignment; Screening and accession negotiations; Environmental governance and implementation; Waste-management legislation; Biodiversity and nature-conservation legislation; The Natura 2000 framework; Water protection; Air-quality legislation; Climate-change policy; Environmental impact assessment; Strategic environmental assessment; Access to environmental information; and The practical implementation of EU environmental requirements. The Academy is intended to develop both theoretical understanding and practical capacity. Participants will study the legal requirements of EU accession while also considering how environmental legislation can be implemented through national, regional and local institutions. EU Environment Academy 2026–2027 at a Glance Programme: EU Environment Academy 2026–2027 Host country: Ukraine Organiser and funder: Swedish Environmental Protection Agency Application status: Open Application deadline: 20 August 2026 Expected selection date: By 10 September 2026 Programme period: Approximately late September 2026 to March 2027 Winter break: Included Primary format: Online In-person component: One or two possible study visits or workshops Possible study-visit locations: Poland, Sweden or Belgium, including Brussels Working language: English Expected workload: Approximately 10 hours per week Number of participants: Approximately 30 Participation costs: Fully covered by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency Application method: Letter of Intent submitted by email Application email: EUacademy@swedishepa.se Qualification awarded: Certificate for successful completion Post-programme opportunity: Access to the EU Environment Academy alumni network Programme Duration and Format The EU Environment Academy will run for approximately six months, from late September 2026 until March 2027. A winter break will be included in the schedule. The programme will be delivered primarily online through live sessions. The learning format is expected to combine: Live lectures; Interactive case studies; Group exercises; Individual assignments; Guided self-study; Practical exercises; Independent reading; and Examination sessions. Online delivery will allow participants from different parts of Ukraine to participate while continuing their professional or academic responsibilities. However, the programme requires a substantial weekly commitment. Participants should expect to dedicate approximately 10 hours each week to lectures, assignments, self-study and examinations. Applicants should therefore obtain their employer’s support before applying and ensure that they can consistently allocate sufficient time to the programme. In-Person Study Visits and Workshops Although the Academy will be conducted mainly online, the programme may include one or two face-to-face study visits or workshops. These events are expected to be arranged in European Union Member States that are geographically close to Ukraine or particularly relevant to the programme. The official announcement identifies the following possible locations: Poland; Sweden; or Belgium, particularly Brussels. The final number, location and schedule of the face-to-face activities have not yet been confirmed. The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency states that participation costs will be fully covered, including costs related to face-to-face events. However, the official page does not provide a detailed breakdown of individual travel, accommodation, insurance or visa arrangements. Selected participants should therefore obtain specific guidance from the programme organisers before making travel arrangements. Participation Costs and Employer Responsibilities There is no participation fee for selected candidates. The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency will fully cover participation costs, including costs connected with the programme’s face-to-face activities. While the programme is funded, employers are expected to support participating employees in two important ways: Allocation of working time Employers must allow selected participants to attend webinars, lectures and other programme activities during working hours. Provision of technical equipment Employers should provide the technical equipment required for online participation, including a suitable computer and camera. Candidates who are selected will be required to submit confirmation from their employer stating that they will receive sufficient working time to complete the course and participate in its online activities. Applicants should discuss this requirement with their employer before applying. A candidate who cannot obtain the required institutional support may face difficulty confirming participation after selection. Programme Language The working language of the EU Environment Academy is English. Applicants should indicate their English-language level in their application. A good command of English will be beneficial because the curriculum involves lectures, EU legal terminology, academic materials, assignments, case studies and examinations. The organisers state that simultaneous interpretation may be offered during webinars. However, interpretation is described as a possibility rather than a guaranteed service for every activity. Applicants should therefore be prepared to study and communicate in English. Understanding Chapter 27 of the EU Acquis Chapter 27 is the part of the EU accession framework dealing with environmental and climate-related legislation. Candidate countries must align their national laws, administrative arrangements and implementation systems with the relevant European Union requirements. For Ukraine, this process requires more than formally adopting new laws. Government institutions, environmental authorities and other organisations must also develop the ability to implement, monitor and enforce those requirements. The EU Environment Academy therefore focuses on both legislation and practical application. It aims to help participants understand: What EU environmental law requires; How EU legislation is developed; How directives and regulations operate; How candidate countries approximate national laws with EU law; How accession screening and negotiations are conducted; Which institutions are responsible for implementation; What administrative capacity is needed; How environmental obligations affect national and local authorities; and How civil society and professional organisations can contribute to environmental governance. Detailed Programme Structure The programme is divided into three modules covering the EU legal system, accession procedures and environmental legislation. Module One: EU Acquis and the EU Legal and Institutional Framework The first module provides an introduction to the institutional and legal foundations of the European Union. Participants will study the different EU institutions, bodies and agencies, their responsibilities and how they operate together. The module will also examine how EU institutions interact with the authorities of Member States and candidate countries. The legal component is expected to address: Primary EU law, including treaties; Secondary legislation; Legislative acts; Executive and implementing acts; Communications; Conclusions; Resolutions; Reports; Other non-binding instruments; The principle of primacy of EU law; and The direct effect of EU law. The module will use online lectures, group case studies, self-study activities, assignments and practical exercises to help participants understand how EU laws and policies are developed and applied. Module Two: Understanding the EU Accession Process The second module provides a more detailed examination of EU enlargement and accession. Its purpose is to strengthen participants’ ability to understand, prepare for and contribute to the accession process. It is particularly relevant to public officials and professionals whose work involves legislative approximation, regulatory reform, environmental policy or accession negotiations. Topics are expected to include: EU enlargement policy; The EU’s revised enlargement methodology; Legal and institutional approximation; Development of an approximation strategy; Screening of national legislation; Structure of accession negotiations; Preparation for negotiations; Participation in negotiation processes; and Institutional responsibilities during accession. The module will help participants understand the steps through which candidate countries examine existing national laws, identify gaps and introduce reforms required for compliance with EU legislation. Module Three: Chapter 27 of the EU Environmental Acquis The third and largest module focuses on EU environmental legislation under Chapter 27. It will provide participants with an extensive overview of the directives and regulations that candidate countries must integrate into their national systems. While the programme will examine the broader scope of Chapter 27, particular attention will be given to waste management, biodiversity conservation and practical implementation. The detailed curriculum presented on the programme page covers both horizontal and sector-specific environmental legislation. Horizontal environmental legislation The horizontal component may include: Environmental Impact Assessment; Strategic Environmental Assessment; The Aarhus Convention; Public participation in environmental decision-making; Access to environmental information; and Cross-cutting principles of environmental governance. Waste-management legislation Waste management is identified as one of the programme’s priority areas. Participants will examine relevant EU directives and regulations and consider the institutional and practical requirements for their implementation. Biodiversity and nature conservation The biodiversity component will include the EU’s nature-protection framework, particularly: The Birds Directive; The Habitats Directive; Natura 2000; Protected areas; National parks; and Institutional responsibilities for biodiversity conservation. Air quality The curriculum description includes EU legislation concerning ambient air quality and cleaner air, including Directive 2008/50/EC. Water protection Participants will study the EU’s approach to water protection and the legislative responsibilities that candidate countries must incorporate into national governance systems. Access to environmental information The programme will consider the first pillar of the Aarhus Convention and Directive 2003/4/EC concerning public access to environmental information. Climate change and the European Green Deal A portion of the module will address climate-change legislation and the importance of the European Green Deal. The course will also examine connections between environmental requirements and other areas of EU law, including: Chapter 15 on Energy; and Chapter 11 on Agriculture. Gender equality, equity and environmental policy are also identified among the subjects covered in the detailed programme description. Expected Learning Outcomes By completing the EU Environment Academy, participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of the overall EU environmental acquis and the accession negotiation process. The programme is designed to strengthen participants’ ability to: Understand the legal and institutional structure of the European Union; Interpret EU environmental legislation; Follow developments in EU law and policy; Analyse the requirements of Chapter 27; Understand legislative approximation; Contribute to accession preparation and negotiations; Identify gaps between national and EU legislation; Address environmental governance challenges; Solve professional problems independently; Apply knowledge within government, civil society or academic work; and Support the practical implementation of environmental legislation. The course can help prepare participants for qualified roles in national, regional and local government agencies, professional and public-interest organisations, civil society and international organisations. Certificate and Alumni Network Participants who successfully complete the programme will receive a certificate. Successful participants will also be invited to join the EU Environment Academy alumni network. The network is intended to support continuing professional contact, knowledge exchange and cooperation among people working on EU approximation and environmental governance. Alumni activities may include: Tailored seminars on EU accession; Online lectures; Knowledge-sharing activities; Continued dialogue among participants; Exchange of professional experience; Invitations to relevant local or regional events; and Opportunities to maintain contact with other members of the course. The alumni network is intended to remain useful after the formal course has ended by providing a professional platform for discussing EU environmental legislation and implementation. Who Can Apply? The EU Environment Academy 2026 is open to people in Ukraine who work in the environmental field within government agencies and other relevant institutions. Potential applicants include professionals working in: Government ministries; Central government agencies; Regional authorities; Local authorities; Environmental institutions; Non-governmental organisations; Civil-society organisations; and Other institutions whose daily work is substantially affected by EU accession requirements. Advanced-level university students specialising in EU accession, environmental studies or a closely related field may also be considered. Academic and Professional Requirements Applicants are expected to meet the following requirements: Be based in Ukraine; Work in the environmental field or in a role substantially affected by EU accession; Alternatively, be an advanced-level university student in a relevant field; Hold at least a bachelor’s degree from a university in a related discipline; Possess knowledge of English; Be able to commit approximately 10 hours each week; Have access to the technical equipment needed for online participation; and Be able to obtain employer confirmation if selected. The official announcement does not specify a minimum academic grade, a required number of years of professional experience or a formal English-language test score. Selection Process Approximately 30 participants will be selected. Selection will be based on the Letter of Intent submitted by each applicant. The programme will give priority to younger candidates who are at the beginning of their professional careers. However, the organisers also aim to create a balanced group containing participants with different ages and levels of professional experience. Early-career priority should therefore not be interpreted as a strict age limit or as an automatic exclusion of experienced professionals. The organisers aim to complete the selection process by 10 September 2026. Candidates who are selected must subsequently provide confirmation from their employer that they will be allowed to use working time to participate in the programme’s webinars, lectures and other activities. How to Apply There is no online application form listed for the current programme. Applicants must submit a Letter of Intent by email. Application email EUacademy@swedishepa.se Letter of Intent requirements The Letter of Intent must not exceed two A4 pages. It should explain: Where the applicant works; The applicant’s current professional role; How the applicant’s work relates to EU approximation; The applicant’s general knowledge and experience in the environmental field; The applicant’s academic qualifications and merits; and The applicant’s motivation for joining the EU Environment Academy. Applicants should also indicate their level of English, as requested in the programme’s language guidance. The Letter of Intent is the main document used to evaluate applicants. It should therefore provide specific evidence of professional responsibilities, environmental knowledge and involvement in work connected with EU accession or legislative approximation. How to Prepare a Strong Letter of Intent A competitive Letter of Intent should be clear, specific and directly connected to the Academy’s objectives. Applicants should consider the following approach: 1. Introduce the professional context State the organisation, department, current position and principal responsibilities. Avoid giving only a job title without explaining the work performed. 2. Explain the connection with EU approximation Describe how the applicant’s work is affected by Ukraine’s EU accession process. Strong applications should identify specific policies, regulations, programmes or institutional responsibilities related to environmental alignment. 3. Demonstrate environmental knowledge Provide concrete examples of work involving environmental legislation, waste management, biodiversity, climate policy, water, air quality, environmental assessment or another relevant field. 4. Present academic qualifications Briefly identify relevant degrees, courses, research or professional training. Only qualifications that support the application should be emphasised. 5. Explain the motivation Describe why the programme is important to the applicant’s current responsibilities and future professional contribution. The motivation should go beyond general interest in Europe or the environment. 6. Explain the expected institutional value Show how the knowledge acquired will be used after the course. This could include supporting policy development, legislative alignment, implementation, institutional capacity, public administration or civil-society engagement. 7. Respect the two-page limit The Letter of Intent must not exceed two A4 pages. Applicants should remove repetition and prioritise evidence directly relevant to the programme. Application Timeline Applications open: Confirmed as open on the official programme page Application deadline: 20 August 2026 Expected completion of selection: By 10 September 2026 Programme commencement: Approximately late September 2026 Winter break: Included Programme completion: Approximately March 2027 Possible study visits or workshops: Dates and locations to be confirmed About the European Institute of Public Administration The official Academy page also provides background information on the European Institute of Public Administration. EIPA is an educational institution specialising in European Union legislation, public affairs and legislative approximation. It has approximately 40 years of experience in training public-administration officials from EU Member States, candidate countries, the European Commission and other EU institutions. Its work combines theoretical understanding with practical knowledge of European Union policies. EIPA has also maintained a substantial presence in countries preparing for EU membership. Official Programme Link Complete programme information and any subsequent updates are available on the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency’s EU Environment Academy 2026 webpage . Conclusion The EU Environment Academy 2026–2027 offers environmental professionals and selected advanced university students in Ukraine an intensive opportunity to develop practical knowledge of European Union environmental law, accession procedures and legislative approximation. With participation costs fully covered, online delivery, possible study visits to EU Member States, a structured three-module curriculum, professional certification and access to an alumni network, the Academy is particularly valuable for people whose work will contribute to Ukraine’s environmental reforms and European integration. The programme requires a serious commitment of approximately 10 hours per week, strong institutional support and a carefully prepared Letter of Intent. Interested candidates should discuss participation with their employer, prepare a focused application of no more than two A4 pages and submit it to EUacademy@swedishepa.se no later than 20 August 2026. title: YEDx 2026 Applications Open: Host a Youth Environmental Dialogue with UNEP’s Children and Youth Major Group (CYMG)
summary: The YEDx 2026 Application is now open for youth organizations and environmental groups worldwide interested in hosting a Youth Environmental Dialogue (YEDx) in partnership with the Children and Youth Major Group to the United Nations Environment Programme (CYMG) . This opportunity provides young environmental leaders and organizations with the chance to organize locally led dialogues that bridge international environmental governance with grassroots youth action. Selected hosts will receive mentorship, guidance, practical toolkits, and ongoing support from CYMG while leading meaningful environmental conversations in their own communities. As environmental challenges continue to intensify across the globe, young people are increasingly recognized as critical drivers of sustainable solutions. Through YEDx, CYMG seeks to empower youth to transform international environmental commitments into tangible local action while ensuring that local experiences help shape global environmental policies. Whether you represent a youth organization, environmental NGO, university group, community-based organization, or another youth-serving institution, this initiative offers an excellent opportunity to become part of an international movement advancing environmental leadership and meaningful youth participation. What is the Children and Youth Major Group (CYMG)? The Children and Youth Major Group (CYMG) serves as the official youth engagement mechanism to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) . Established following the 1992 Rio Earth Summit (Agenda 21) , CYMG represents youth organizations, networks, and individuals committed to addressing the world s most pressing environmental challenges. CYMG actively advocates for stronger youth participation in environmental governance by ensuring young people s voices are represented throughout UNEP processes and wider United Nations environmental discussions. Today, the organization continues to strengthen youth leadership while promoting meaningful participation in global environmental decision-making. Its work focuses primarily on addressing the world s triple planetary crisis , including: Climate change Biodiversity loss Pollution By creating opportunities such as YEDx, CYMG helps equip young leaders with the knowledge, networks, and resources necessary to implement environmental solutions within their own communities. What is YEDx? Youth Environmental Dialogues (YEDx) are locally organized, youth-led events designed to connect international environmental policy discussions with practical community action. Rather than being centrally organized by UNEP, YEDx events empower local organizations to take ownership of planning and delivering meaningful environmental dialogues while receiving support from CYMG. Each YEDx creates a platform where young people can: Learn about global environmental governance. Discuss local environmental challenges. Develop practical solutions. Connect with policymakers and community stakeholders. Build stronger youth environmental networks. Contribute local perspectives to international environmental discussions. The initiative recognizes that many environmental challenges require local solutions informed by global knowledge. Objectives of YEDx 2026 Every Youth Environmental Dialogue is designed around four primary objectives. 1. Equip Young People with Leadership Skills YEDx aims to strengthen the knowledge and leadership capacity of young environmental advocates by providing opportunities to develop practical skills that support environmental action. Participants are encouraged to become active changemakers capable of leading sustainability initiatives within their communities. 2. Increase Awareness of Global Environmental Policies The programme helps young people better understand major international environmental frameworks and policies. By improving awareness of global commitments, participants are better equipped to implement local initiatives that contribute toward broader environmental goals. 3. Elevate Local Youth Voices One of the central purposes of YEDx is ensuring that local youth perspectives help shape international environmental conversations. Insights gathered during local dialogues can contribute to broader discussions taking place within UNEP and other global environmental forums. 4. Strengthen Environmental Networks YEDx encourages collaboration among young leaders, organizations, institutions, and community stakeholders. These partnerships support long-term environmental advocacy and strengthen collective efforts to address local environmental challenges. How Does YEDx Work? One of the unique aspects of YEDx is its emphasis on local leadership . Selected organizations are responsible for designing and delivering their own Youth Environmental Dialogue while receiving continuous guidance from CYMG. Responsibilities of Local Hosts Selected organizers will: Coordinate the entire YEDx event. Engage local youth participants. Build partnerships with local organizations. Organize event logistics. Facilitate discussions. Promote community participation. Deliver activities aligned with YEDx objectives. Support Provided by CYMG Throughout the planning process, CYMG provides: Ongoing mentorship. Technical advice. Capacity-building opportunities. Ready-made planning toolkits. Guidance for successful implementation. Support throughout the event planning process. This collaborative model enables local organizers to tailor each dialogue to their community while maintaining alignment with international environmental priorities. Why Host a YEDx? Hosting a Youth Environmental Dialogue offers numerous benefits for organizations and youth leaders. Potential advantages include: Leading environmental change within your community. Strengthening organizational leadership experience. Connecting local environmental work with international policy discussions. Building partnerships with environmental stakeholders. Increasing youth participation in environmental governance. Enhancing organizational visibility. Developing long-term environmental advocacy initiatives. Accessing mentorship from experienced environmental leaders. Becoming part of a global network of youth environmental changemakers. Who Can Host a YEDx? CYMG welcomes applications from eligible organizations committed to youth engagement and environmental action. Eligible applicants may include: Youth-led organizations. Youth-serving organizations. Environmental organizations. Climate organizations. Community-based organizations. Student organizations. University groups. Academic institutions. Other organizations working with young people and sustainability. Applicants must either: Be affiliated with a legally registered eligible organization; or Partner with a registered organization capable of supporting the event. Application Requirements Applicants will be asked to provide information including: Primary applicant details. Date of birth. Nationality. Organization name. Organization type. Country of operation. Year established. Registration status. Organization website or social media. Partner organization information (if applicable). Secondary contact details. Applicants should carefully complete every required section before submission. APPLY NOW Application Deadline Applications have been extended until 16 August 2026. Selection Process Submitting an application does not guarantee selection. All applications will undergo review by a CYMG Selection Committee . Applications will be evaluated using the official selection criteria outlined in the YEDx Guidelines 2026 . Organizations are encouraged to review these guidelines thoroughly before applying to strengthen their application. Important Notes Applicants should keep in mind: Hosting opportunities are competitive. Local organizers lead the implementation. CYMG provides mentorship and planning resources. Applications are reviewed through a formal selection process. Partnerships with registered organizations are accepted where necessary. Need Assistance? Applicants with questions regarding the programme or application process may contact CYMG directly via: Email: admin@cymgenv.net Conclusion The YEDx 2026 Host Opportunity represents an exciting chance for youth organizations and environmental leaders worldwide to play a direct role in strengthening environmental governance from the grassroots level. By combining local leadership with global environmental priorities, YEDx empowers young people to create lasting environmental impact while contributing valuable perspectives to international policy discussions. Organizations passionate about youth engagement, sustainability, and community action are encouraged to prepare strong applications and review the official YEDx Guidelines 2026 carefully before submitting. Hosting a YEDx is more than organizing an event—it is an opportunity to inspire environmental leadership, strengthen community collaboration, and help shape a more sustainable future. title: University of Washington International Program in Public Health Leadership (IPPHL) 2027: Fully Funded Leadership Fellowship for African Public Health Professionals
summary: The University of Washington International Program in Public Health Leadership (IPPHL) 2027 is now accepting applications from mid-career public health professionals across Africa. Designed specifically for emerging leaders working in or closely with African Ministries of Health, this prestigious fully funded leadership program equips participants with the knowledge, leadership skills, and policy expertise needed to strengthen health systems and drive sustainable public health transformation. Hosted by the Evans School of Public Policy Governance at the University of Washington , the International Program in Public Health Leadership is supported by the Bill Melinda Gates Foundation and delivered in partnership with the Center for Creative Leadership . Over the course of eight months, participants engage in an intensive leadership development experience that combines policy analysis, implementation science, evidence-based decision-making, and personal leadership growth. Since its launch in 2017 , the program has graduated 227 public health professionals representing 34 African countries , creating a growing network of leaders committed to improving health outcomes across the continent. If you are an experienced public health professional working within government or in close partnership with government health systems in Africa, this opportunity provides world-class leadership training with financial support and international networking opportunities. What is the University of Washington International Program in Public Health Leadership? The International Program in Public Health Leadership (IPPHL) is a flagship executive leadership program developed to strengthen leadership capacity among professionals responsible for shaping public health policies and managing health programs throughout Africa. Unlike traditional academic degrees, IPPHL is a highly practical leadership initiative designed to help participants: Strengthen policy leadership skills Improve evidence-based decision-making Develop effective public health implementation strategies Enhance organizational leadership capabilities Build sustainable health system solutions Create lasting policy impact within their respective countries Participants continue contributing to their organizations while completing an intensive eight-month curriculum focused on solving real public health challenges. About the University of Washington The University of Washington is one of the world s leading public research universities, internationally recognized for excellence in education, policy research, medicine, and public health. Through the Evans School of Public Policy Governance, the university has developed IPPHL to strengthen leadership within African health systems by investing in professionals capable of influencing policy and improving health outcomes at national and regional levels. Program Objectives The program aims to produce stronger public health leaders who can: Design evidence-based public policies Improve implementation of health programs Lead organizational and institutional change Strengthen health system performance Build sustainable policy solutions Improve health outcomes for communities Develop stronger leadership practices within government institutions Program Curriculum Participants will complete an intensive curriculum covering several core areas of leadership and policy development. 1. Public Policy Analysis Participants learn how to: Analyze public policies Develop policy recommendations Evaluate policy effectiveness Apply evidence in policymaking 2. Evidence and Evaluation The curriculum develops participants ability to: Interpret research findings Use health data effectively Evaluate public health interventions Make evidence-informed decisions 3. Policy Implementation Participants strengthen their understanding of: Program implementation Change management Public sector leadership Health system improvement Implementation science 4. Personal Leadership Development The program also emphasizes leadership growth through: Executive leadership coaching Leadership reflection Communication skills Strategic thinking Team leadership Decision-making Organizational influence Fully Funded Benefits One of the most attractive features of IPPHL is that it is fully funded by the Gates Foundation . There are: No application fees No tuition fees No program fees The program also covers most major participation costs, including: Lodging during the two-week Leadership Immersion Airfare for the Leadership Immersion Lodging during the one-week Capstone Seminar Airfare for the Capstone Seminar Participants also receive limited financial support for certain additional expenses. Participant Expenses While the program covers most major costs, participants are expected to pay for certain expenses, including: Visa fees Internet connectivity Other minor participation-related costs Limited financial assistance is available to help offset these expenses during or after completion of the program. Who Should Apply? The University of Washington is seeking experienced public health professionals who are already making important contributions within government health systems across Africa. title: Scottish Government Launches Global Solidarity Fund 2026: Apply for Grants of Up to £50,000 to Support International Development and Global Citizenship
summary: The Scottish Government has officially launched the Global Solidarity Fund (GSF) , a new funding programme designed to strengthen Scotland s contribution to international development and global citizenship. Applications are now open for eligible Scottish-based organizations seeking financial support to expand their impact, strengthen their institutions, and build more equitable partnerships with communities around the world. The Global Solidarity Fund has been created to make government funding more accessible, particularly for smaller organizations, community groups, and diaspora-led initiatives that may have limited experience applying for public funding. Through this initiative, the Scottish Government aims to empower organizations that are making meaningful contributions to sustainable development, global solidarity, and international cooperation. With grants ranging from £2,000 to £50,000 , the programme offers flexible funding opportunities across three different grant streams, allowing organizations to apply for support that best matches their goals and stage of development. About the Global Solidarity Fund The Global Solidarity Fund is a Scottish Government initiative that supports organizations working to address global challenges through international development and global citizenship activities. Rather than focusing solely on financial assistance, the programme seeks to strengthen organizations, encourage locally led development, and promote greater public awareness of global issues. The fund recognizes the important role that small organizations, charities, community groups, and diaspora communities play in building lasting international partnerships and delivering sustainable development outcomes. A key objective of the fund is to remove barriers that often prevent smaller organizations from accessing government grants. The programme has therefore been designed to be straightforward, supportive, and particularly welcoming to first-time applicants. Funding Streams Available Applicants may apply under one of three funding streams, depending on the nature of their organization and project. 1. Scottish Civil Society Organisation (CSO) Strengthening Grant Maximum Grant: Up to £10,000 This funding stream is designed to strengthen the capacity of small Scottish-based civil society organizations. The grant supports organizations in becoming: Safer More resilient Better governed More effective Better equipped to deliver their mission The funding is available for Scottish-based CSOs working in countries classified as having medium or low levels of development. Global Citizenship Engagement Grant Maximum Grant: Up to £5,000 for small charities and social enterprises Up to £2,000 for unaffiliated groups This funding stream supports projects that increase public awareness and engagement with global citizenship. Projects may focus on: Public education Community engagement Awareness campaigns Learning activities Events promoting global citizenship Educational initiatives that encourage international understanding Although the primary focus is on Scotland, the programme is not limited exclusively to Scottish audiences. 3. The grant seeks to strengthen partnerships where local organizations play a leading role in identifying priorities and implementing solutions that best meet the needs of their communities. Eligible applicants include: Scottish civil society organizations Small charities Social enterprises Community groups Diaspora-led organizations Scottish international NGOs Organizations new to Scottish Government funding The programme is particularly suitable for smaller organizations looking to expand their impact while building stronger institutional capacity. title: U.S. Embassy Ghana Public Diplomacy Grants Program 2026: Apply for Grants of Up to $60,000 to Strengthen U.S.-Ghana Relations
summary: The U.S. Embassy in Accra , through its Public Diplomacy Section , has announced applications for the 2026 Public Diplomacy Grants Program , inviting eligible organizations to submit innovative project proposals that strengthen the long-standing partnership between Ghana and the United States. The program seeks initiatives that advance mutual understanding, democratic values, education, entrepreneurship, innovation, media development, cultural exchange, and inclusive economic growth. Funded by the U.S. Department of State , the program provides grants ranging from $15,000 to $60,000 for projects that align with U.S. foreign policy priorities and promote collaboration between Ghanaian and American institutions and communities. Approximately $120,000 is available for this funding cycle, with between two and eight awards expected to be made. Projects should have a duration of three to ten months and begin within 90 days of the award date . This grant opportunity is particularly significant as it supports activities celebrating the 250th anniversary of the United States independence (Freedom 250) and the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Ghana and the United States , encouraging projects that deepen cooperation while creating lasting impact across Ghana. About the U.S. Embassy Ghana Public Diplomacy Grants Program The Public Diplomacy Grants Program is an annual funding initiative designed to strengthen the relationship between Ghana and the United States through people-to-people engagement, institutional partnerships, and community-based initiatives. Rather than supporting charitable or humanitarian assistance, the program focuses on activities that promote dialogue, education, innovation, leadership, cultural understanding, and democratic participation. Successful projects are expected to create measurable outcomes while reinforcing the shared interests and values of both countries. Funding Details Applicants should take note of the following funding information: Funding Opportunity: Public Diplomacy Grants/Small Grants Program – Ghana (FY2026) Grant Amount: Approximately $15,000–$60,000 Total Funding Available: Approximately $120,000 Expected Number of Awards: 2–8 Project Duration: 3–10 months Project Start: Within 90 days after award Funding Source: U.S. Department of State Public Diplomacy Funds The Embassy reserves the right to make fewer or more awards depending on funding availability and the quality of applications received. Program Objectives The Embassy seeks projects that directly support one or more of the following objectives: Strengthen U.S.-Ghana bilateral relations. Promote democratic governance and civic participation. Celebrate Freedom 250 and the 70th anniversary of U.S.-Ghana diplomatic relations. Encourage entrepreneurship and innovation. Expand educational opportunities and academic collaboration. Promote STEM education. Support independent and responsible journalism. Strengthen media literacy. Promote religious tolerance and interfaith dialogue. Enhance economic prosperity and workforce development. Encourage youth leadership and civic engagement. Promote American culture, values, and institutions. Foster sustainable institutional partnerships between Ghanaian and American organizations. Types of Projects That May Be Funded Applicants are encouraged to design creative projects that align with the Embassy s priorities. Examples include: Conferences and symposiums Workshops and seminars Academic lectures Speaker programs Professional training Journalism capacity-building programs Entrepreneurship boot camps Innovation competitions STEM education initiatives Cultural exhibitions Artistic performances Community outreach campaigns Leadership development programs Alumni engagement activities Professional exchange initiatives Public awareness campaigns Networking events Research and policy dialogue initiatives Who Can Apply? The opportunity is open to eligible organizations capable of managing U.S. government grant funding. Eligible applicants include: Registered nonprofit organizations Civil society organizations Educational institutions Universities Think tanks Public international organizations Government institutions Independent media organizations Cultural organizations Applicants should demonstrate sound financial management systems, experienced personnel, and the organizational capacity to successfully implement the proposed project. Target Beneficiaries Projects may focus on a variety of audiences, including: Youth (14–35 years) Secondary school students University students Young professionals Entrepreneurs Journalists Government officials Policymakers Civil society leaders Religious leaders Researchers Academic institutions Alumni of U.S. Government exchange programs Communities throughout Ghana The Embassy encourages projects that reach participants across the country, with particular attention to major population centers and regional capitals. Application Requirements A complete application package must include all required forms and supporting documents. Applicants are expected to provide: A detailed project narrative. A comprehensive implementation timeline. A monitoring and evaluation (M E) plan. A detailed budget and budget justification. Organizational documentation. Financial management information. Required certifications and assurances. Any additional documents requested by the Embassy. Applications missing required documentation will be considered technically ineligible and will not proceed to the review stage. Registration Requirements Before receiving an award, applicants are generally expected to obtain: A Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) . An active System for Award Management (SAM.gov) registration. Because these registrations can take four to eight weeks , organizations are encouraged to begin the process as early as possible. Funding Restrictions Certain costs and activities are not eligible for funding under this program. These include: Construction activities or construction costs. Direct social welfare or charitable assistance. Medical assistance or projects involving medical professionals such as doctors, nurses, or psychiatrists delivering healthcare services. Pre-award costs without prior approval. Alcoholic beverages. Entertainment expenses unrelated to project objectives. Purchases or operation of prohibited unmanned aircraft systems. Activities that violate applicable U.S. laws, regulations, or Executive Orders. How Applications Will Be Evaluated Eligible applications will be scored using the following criteria: Quality and Feasibility of the Program Idea (30 points) – Innovation, relevance, feasibility, implementation plan, and alignment with program priorities. Organizational Capacity and Previous Grant Performance (25 points) – Organizational expertise, financial management, staffing, partnerships, and grant management experience. Project Planning and Ability to Achieve Objectives (20 points) – Clear objectives, implementation strategy, participant recruitment, geographic coverage, and realistic timelines. Budget (10 points) – Reasonableness, cost-effectiveness, and detailed budget justification. Monitoring and Evaluation (10 points) – Measurable outputs, outcomes, indicators, and evaluation framework. Sustainability (5 points) – Plans to sustain project outcomes beyond the funding period. Review and Award Process The review process includes several stages: Confirmation of application receipt. Technical eligibility screening. Independent review by a technical panel. Risk assessment of shortlisted applicants, including financial stability, management systems, and previous performance. Notification of results, generally within 120 days after the application deadline . Successful applicants may also undergo Risk Analysis Management (RAM) vetting , requiring submission of additional information for key personnel through the Department of State s secure portal. Reporting and Compliance Requirements Grant recipients will be required to: Submit quarterly program progress reports. Submit quarterly financial reports. Submit final programmatic and financial reports. Maintain appropriate accounting records. Report foreign assistance data where applicable. Comply with U.S. Department of State branding and marking requirements. Use Freedom 250 logos on eligible project materials where required. Budget Guidance Applicants should prepare detailed budgets covering items such as: Personnel and fringe benefits. Travel and per diem. Equipment. Supplies. Contractual services. Other direct costs. Indirect costs. Cost sharing or in-kind contributions. Each cost category should be clearly justified, and applicants requesting indirect costs should provide the necessary supporting documentation if applicable. Application Deadline Deadline: August 14, 2026 Applications must be submitted on or before the stated deadline. The Embassy also requires questions regarding the funding opportunity to be submitted by the same deadline, as specified in the Annual Program Statement. Official Resources For complete application guidelines and supporting documents, visit the official U.S. Embassy Ghana website: Official Website: U.S. Embassy Ghana – Public Diplomacy Grants You can access the following official documents on the website: Annual Program Statement for Public Diplomacy Application Format / Project Proposal Template Budget Narrative Sample Template Applicants are strongly encouraged to review these documents carefully before preparing and submitting their proposals to ensure compliance with all application requirements. Conclusion The 2026 U.S. Embassy Ghana Public Diplomacy Grants Program offers a valuable opportunity for eligible organizations to secure funding for projects that strengthen U.S.-Ghana relations and address shared priorities in education, innovation, democracy, entrepreneurship, media, culture, and community engagement. By supporting high-impact initiatives with sustainable outcomes, the program aims to foster stronger institutional partnerships, empower communities, and promote mutual understanding between the people of Ghana and the United States. Organizations with innovative ideas, sound management systems, and the capacity to deliver measurable results are encouraged to prepare strong proposals and submit complete applications before the deadline. title: Call for Applications: Early-Career Researchers Invited to Review the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report AR7 Draft
summary: Registration is now open for experts to participate in the review of the First Order Draft of the Working Group I contribution to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Seventh Assessment Report . The Working Group I contribution to the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report, commonly referred to as AR7, will assess the latest scientific understanding of the physical basis of climate change. It will examine observed and projected climate changes, climate-system processes and feedbacks, and regional climate information. Researchers and professionals with relevant expertise are invited to register as expert reviewers and contribute comments during the official review period, which runs from 10 August to 2 October 2026 . The deadline to register as an expert reviewer is 25 September 2026 at 23:50 Central European Summer Time . Although early-career researchers are encouraged to participate where their expertise is relevant, the updated call is open to qualified experts more broadly and is not limited to a coordinated early-career group-review programme. About the IPCC Expert Review The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is the United Nations body responsible for assessing scientific knowledge related to climate change. Rather than conducting original research, the IPCC evaluates and synthesises the existing scientific literature to provide governments and policymakers with comprehensive assessments of: The physical science of climate change Climate impacts, adaptation and vulnerability Climate-change mitigation Scientific uncertainties and knowledge gaps Regional and global climate risks The Seventh Assessment Report is being developed through a structured drafting and review process involving scientists, researchers and experts from around the world. The First Order Draft is an early version of the Working Group I report. Expert review is an essential part of the IPCC assessment process because it allows specialists to examine the draft, identify gaps or inaccuracies, recommend relevant literature and help ensure that the final report is scientifically rigorous, balanced and transparent. This is the first of several review stages planned during the preparation of the Working Group I contribution to AR7. What the Working Group I Report Covers Working Group I focuses on the physical science basis of climate change . Its contribution to the Seventh Assessment Report will assess areas including: Observed changes in the global climate system Projected future climate change Large-scale climate patterns and trends Climate processes and feedbacks Interactions among the atmosphere, oceans, land and cryosphere Regional climate information Climate variability Extreme events Scientific uncertainties Evidence from observations, modelling and paleoclimate research Prospective reviewers should consult the official report outline before registering. The outline can help experts determine whether their academic, scientific or professional background is relevant to a particular chapter or topic. View the Working Group I report outline: CLICK HERE Benefits of Participating Participating in the IPCC expert-review process provides an opportunity to contribute directly to one of the world’s most influential climate-science assessments. Expert reviewers can: Contribute specialist knowledge to the assessment process Examine how current climate research is represented in the draft Identify missing, outdated or incorrectly interpreted scientific evidence Recommend relevant peer-reviewed literature Comment on the clarity, balance and scientific accuracy of draft sections Gain insight into how major international climate assessments are developed Support the production of evidence used in global climate-policy discussions Strengthen their understanding of international scientific assessment processes The review is not a conventional peer-review assignment for a single academic article. Reviewers may be assessing a large, interdisciplinary report intended to synthesise extensive bodies of scientific evidence for policymakers and other users. Comments should therefore be precise, evidence-based and directly relevant to the text being reviewed. Who Can Apply? Registration is open to experts whose knowledge and experience are relevant to the Working Group I assessment. Potential reviewers may include: University researchers Independent scientists Government researchers Specialists from research institutes Climate-modelling experts Earth-system scientists Meteorologists Oceanographers Cryosphere and polar researchers Atmospheric scientists Paleoclimate researchers Regional climate specialists Professionals with relevant technical expertise Advanced early-career researchers familiar with current scientific literature Early-career researchers may register where they possess sufficient expertise to provide substantive comments on the draft. However, applicants should not interpret the updated call as being restricted to master’s students, doctoral candidates, postdoctoral researchers or scientists within a specified number of years after completing a PhD. The key consideration is whether the reviewer has suitable expertise in topics covered by the Working Group I report. Prospective reviewers should review the official outline carefully before registering. A title, degree or general interest in climate change is not, by itself, a substitute for relevant knowledge of the scientific literature. Review Process and Time Commitment The official expert-review period runs from: 10 August to 2 October 2026 Registered experts will review the First Order Draft and submit comments through the IPCC’s designated review system. The exact time required will depend on: The number of chapters or sections reviewed The reviewer’s area of expertise The technical complexity of the material The amount of supporting literature examined The number and detail of comments submitted Reviewers should allow sufficient time to read the relevant sections carefully, check references and prepare constructive comments. Strong review comments should: Identify the specific chapter, section, paragraph or statement concerned. Explain the scientific issue clearly. Provide supporting reasoning or evidence. Recommend a correction, clarification or relevant source where appropriate. Remain professional, concise and focused on improving the report. The IPCC has also published a mini guide to help expert reviewers understand the process and prepare useful comments. Read the Mini Guide for Expert Reviewers: CLICK HERE Organizations Coordinating the Initiative The review is part of the formal preparation of the Working Group I contribution to the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report . The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change oversees the global assessment process, while Working Group I is responsible for evaluating the physical science basis of climate change. The updated registration call is therefore broader than the earlier coordinated early-career initiative led by scientific networks. Researchers who previously encountered information about an APECS-led group review should rely on the current IPCC registration details and deadlines when seeking to participate in the official expert review. Experts remain responsible for ensuring that participation is consistent with any requirements imposed by their employer, university, research funder, government or institution. Application Deadline The deadline to register as an expert reviewer is: 25 September 2026 at 23:50 CEST The First Order Draft review itself closes on: 2 October 2026 Because registration remains open only shortly before the end of the review period, interested experts should register as early as possible. Waiting until the registration deadline may leave insufficient time to examine the draft and prepare thoughtful, evidence-based comments. International applicants should carefully convert the deadline from Central European Summer Time to their local time zone. How to Apply Interested experts must register through the official expert-review registration portal. Before registering, prospective reviewers should: Consult the Working Group I report outline. Identify the chapters or topics most closely aligned with their expertise. Confirm that they can participate during the review period. Review the expert-review guidance. Complete the official registration process. Follow the instructions provided for accessing and reviewing the draft. Register as an expert reviewer: APPLY HERE Read the full IPCC press release: CLICK HERE Conclusion The expert review of the First Order Draft of the Working Group I contribution to the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report offers qualified researchers and professionals an important opportunity to strengthen the global assessment of climate science. Working Group I will examine the latest evidence concerning observed and projected climate change, climate-system processes, feedbacks and regional climate information. Through the expert-review process, specialists can identify scientific gaps, propose corrections and help ensure that the final assessment accurately reflects the available evidence. The review period runs from 10 August to 2 October 2026 , while expert registration closes on 25 September 2026 at 23:50 CEST . Researchers should consult the official report outline and expert-review guide before registering to ensure that their expertise is relevant and that they can submit a substantive review before the process closes.
